summary:
WaterProof transforms complex NASA NISAR radar observations into accessible evidence for investigating Earth's changing surface. Designed for environmental researchers, it connects interactive geographic exploration with transparent scientific reasoning, helping users move from “something changed” to “what should we investigate next?”

Users can explore real satellite observations through an interactive globe, compare acquisition dates, examine HH and HV radar measurements, and investigate geographically defined candidate regions. A Louisiana demonstration combines six observation dates with change maps, temporal patterns, sensitivity checks, and downloadable investigation notes.

Scientific honesty is central. Darker radar does not automatically mean flooding. WaterProof makes uncertainty visible, distinguishes robust patterns from settings sensitivity and date dependence, and preserves unresolved interpretations. Independent water product comparisons in Thailand and Gandak reveal contrasting performance, demonstrating why results cannot simply transfer between locations.

Built as an open source, interactive research application, WaterProof makes radar data easier to navigate without disguising its limitations. It helps researchers prioritize noteworthy changes, formulate testable questions, and identify the independent evidence needed to understand changing landscapes more responsibly.
details:
WaterProof helps environmental researchers turn complex NASA NISAR radar observations into focused scientific investigations. It addresses a practical challenge: satellite images can reveal striking changes, but understanding what those changes mean requires geographic context, temporal evidence, and an honest assessment of uncertainty.

The application brings these elements together in an interactive research environment. Users can navigate a 3D globe, explore available NISAR observations, compare acquisition dates, inspect geographic change maps, and examine HH and HV radar backscatter. A cached Louisiana demonstration provides six real observation dates, allowing users to follow changes over time and investigate selected regions without repeatedly downloading satellite products.

WaterProof accesses small spatial windows from NISAR GCOV products, checks geographic alignment, excludes invalid pixels, and applies mask-aware filtering to linear radar power before converting it to decibels. Its investigation workflow groups spatially connected changes and prioritizes candidates using documented, descriptive criteria. For each candidate, researchers can inspect its location, observation dates, polarization response, sensitivity to settings, dependence on individual dates, and contrast with surrounding areas. Downloadable research notes preserve the observations, provenance, uncertainties, and suggested next investigation step.

The project’s creative contribution is this connection between visualization and scientific reasoning. A highlighted region becomes a research question supported by an understandable evidence trail. Users can distinguish an observed radar pattern from a proposed environmental explanation and identify the additional evidence needed to investigate it.

Scientific reliability shaped our design. Radar backscatter responds to moisture, vegetation structure, surface roughness, viewing geometry, and processing effects. Consequently, WaterProof does not equate darker pixels with flooding. Independent OPERA water-product comparisons in Thailand and Gandak show that agreement varies substantially across cases. Those results remain explicitly separate from the exploratory Louisiana findings and from the Sentinel-1 benchmark adaptation.

We developed WaterProof using Python, Streamlit, NumPy, SciPy, xarray, h5py, Rasterio, Matplotlib, Folium, and Three.js. ASF search and secure Earthdata access support data discovery and retrieval. Git checkpoints and automated tests support reproducibility and software reliability. AI tools assisted development and documentation; the scientific measurements come from processed satellite observations.

Our intended impact is to reduce the effort required to explore radar data responsibly. With bilingual navigation, clear maps, cached examples, bounded downloads, and exportable evidence, WaterProof helps researchers prioritize noteworthy changes and plan useful follow-up investigations—while keeping the limits of the available evidence visible.
